page.title: Virtual Event Production Company Guide
page.description: Learn what a virtual event production company does, typical costs, timelines, deliverables and how to choose the right partner for your online event.
page.h1: What is a virtual event production company and how do you choose one?
page.definition: A virtual event production company is a specialist crew that runs the broadcast, rehearsal and live operation of online events so the host can focus on content. They own the run of show, manage speakers, operate the streaming encoder and keep a backup stream ready.
page.quick_answer: Hire a production company when you need a live producer, speaker rehearsals, branded graphics, Q&A moderation and a safety net stream. Expect three to four weeks for a webinar and six to eight weeks for a summit.

sections.h2: What does a virtual event production company do?

blocks.p: A production company handles every technical and operational layer of the live event so the host only manages content. They build the run of show, brief and rehearse speakers, operate the platform, moderate Q&A, switch cameras and graphics, monitor a backup stream and deliver an edited recording with clips.

ul: Run of show creation and speaker briefing
Full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go-live
Live producer, platform operator and Q&A moderator during the event
Backup stream monitored throughout the broadcast
Edited recording and highlight clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: How much does virtual event production cost?

blocks.p: Cost depends on format, staffing and platform complexity. Moderated webinars typically range from $2,500 to $7,500 per production. Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions range from $10,000 to $50,000 and above. The platform licence is a separate purchase from the production crew.

sections.h2: What platforms do virtual event production companies support?

blocks.p: Production companies are platform-agnostic; they produce on the software you already use. Common platforms include Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, StreamYard, Livestorm, Cvent, Bizzabo and Goldcast. The production crew brings cameras, encoders, graphics and run-of-show discipline regardless of platform.

ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast for enterprise suites
StreamYard, Livestorm for self-serve monthly plans

sections.h2: What is the typical timeline for a virtual event?

blocks.p: Lead time varies by complexity. A webinar needs three to four weeks from brief to live. A summit or online conference needs six to eight weeks. A hybrid conference should be planned six to eight weeks out with venue AV and platform locked before the agenda is final. A repeat format can move faster.

sections.h2: What deliverables should you expect from a production company?

blocks.p: A professional production package includes pre-event assets, live crew and post-event files. Confirm the list in the statement of work so nothing is assumed.

ul: Run of show document with timing and cues
Speaker brief and rehearsal schedule
Branded slide template and lower-third graphics
Live producer, Q&A moderator and platform operator
Backup stream monitored for the full duration
Edited recording and social-ready clips
Post-event report with attendance and engagement data

sections.h2: How do you evaluate and choose a virtual event production partner?

blocks.p: Ask for a recent show reel, a sample run of show and references from events of similar size and format. Verify they have crew redundancy, a documented backup-stream process and experience on your chosen platform. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

ul: Show reel from the last six months
Sample run of show for your format
References from comparable events
Crew redundancy plan for illness or technical failure
Backup stream workflow documented
Platform-specific certifications or case studies

faq.q: Do I need a production company for a simple Zoom webinar?
faq.a: If you have a single speaker, no slides and no Q&A, you can self-produce. Add a producer when you have multiple speakers, branded graphics, live polling, breakout rooms or a backup stream requirement.

faq.q: Who buys the platform licence, me or the production company?
faq.a: You buy the platform licence. The production company does not sell software; they provide the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream on the platform you choose.
One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event, plus a technical check 60 minutes before go-live. Complex summits may add a speaker-only dry run earlier in the week.

faq.q: What happens if the primary stream fails during the event?
faq.a: The production crew monitors a simultaneous backup stream on a separate encoder or platform. If the primary drops, they switch viewers to the backup with minimal interruption.

faq.q: How fast do I get the recording and clips?
faq.a: Edited recording and highlight clips are delivered within 24 to 48 hours after the event ends, while attendees still remember the content.
